turns.text: Hi, how's everything with you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can't complain.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My flatmate and I keep arguing about who owes what for groceries.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That gets old fast. Would you rather split everything fifty fifty, or each buy your own food and share only basics?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One second, Moshi. Flatmate.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: No worries.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Nina, are you bringing the map or should I?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I've got it on my phone.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's no signal up there though.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I downloaded it, it works offline.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, but I'm bringing the paper one too. Just in case your battery dies.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: You're such a scout. Fine, bring it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Alright, Moshi, conversation over. Go ahead.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Okay. You and your flatmate. Splitting groceries evenly, or going separate?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fifty fifty, I just want peace.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Peace is worth a lot. A shared app that tracks it can stop the arguments too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, next thing. What's a mind map and do they actually help?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's a diagram with the main topic in the middle, and branches going out for ideas and details. Lots of people find them great for seeing connections.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Like a spider web.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. You can use colours, little drawings, and short words instead of full sentences.
